clue.text: Andi Peters can be dull

indicators.note: says the letters of the name could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: the TV presenter's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A jibe that the television presenter Andi Peters is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Andi Peters is a British TV presenter; his full name rearranges into the ten-letter answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means lacking imagination or excitement, a close synonym of dull.

clue.text: Opera text party animal's written up

parts.note: LIB is short for Liberal, a political party

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing a word upwards means the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: Suggests a party-loving creature has been reviewed in an opera programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party animal' looks like one phrase, a reveller, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the words of an opera, sung to the composer's score.

clue.text: Toast secures treat successfully in collapsing hot-dog

indicators.note: the healing word is placed inside the rearranged snack
a collapsing thing falls into disorder, so the letters of the snack are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the six letters of the snack
to treat a patient successfully is to heal them

explanation.surface: Pictures a sausage-in-a-bun falling apart while someone raises a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'Toast' is a drinking salute, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: "Good health!" is a spoken toast made when raising a glass to someone.

clue.text: Shoot scene in mist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to record a scene with a camera
second meaning: a thin haze or cloudy layer

explanation.surface: A director filming a scene on a foggy day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints one foggy shoot, but the camera work and the haze are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to record on camera; the noun also means a thin hazy covering over something.

clue.text: Priest making threats endlessly comes to hitman

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raises Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: says the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: minatory means threatening, menacing

explanation.surface: A clergyman's menacing behaviour ends with him hiring a hitman.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest; MINATORY loses its last letter to leave MINATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eliminator is someone who gets rid of people, a fair description of a contract killer.

clue.text: First for Adam West consuming iron in some drinks?

indicators.note: eating something up means holding it inside
takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: first letter A
first letter W
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Batman actor Adam West taking an iron supplement in his drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam West played Batman in the 1960s TV series; his initials hold the chemical symbol FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having 'a few' is an idiom for drinking several alcoholic drinks, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Band from Skegness ultimately rubbish

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the town is used

parts.note: last letter S
tripe means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of a music group from the seaside town of Skegness.
explanation.walkthrough: Skegness is an English seaside resort; 'Band' suggests musicians but means a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow strip of colour or material, a band across a surface.

clue.text: Cunning leader vanishing in demo

indicators.note: the first letter disappears from the word

parts.note: a demo or demonstration is a protest march

explanation.surface: A sly political leader slips away from a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means knowing, sly or mischievous, as in an arch look.

clue.text: Change test for covering Independent leader

parts.note: to edit is to change text

indicators.note: the exam word goes round the single letter

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Revising an exam for the Independent newspaper's main opinion piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to the paper itself: in newspaper jargon a leader is the editorial column, not a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leader is its leading article, stating the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Safe Tory seats stink

indicators.note: the phrase seats, or holds, the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters running across these two words

explanation.surface: A sneer at Conservative safe seats, accused of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seats' reads as parliamentary constituencies but is the verb: the phrase seats the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetor is a strong, offensive smell, a literary word for a stench.

clue.text: Me about to restrain a drunken Lord Onslow?

indicators.note: the turned word holds the jumbled letters inside
says the two-letter word turns round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone holding back a tipsy aristocrat called Lord Onslow.
explanation.walkthrough: EM holds ARLDO, a jumble of A LORD. Onslow is an earldom in the British peerage; the question mark shows a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Onslow names a peerage title whose holder is an earl, so it is one example of such a rank.

clue.text: Mushy Murphy beaten with one holding ketamine inside?

indicators.note: all of this goes within the potato word

parts.note: a murphy is slang for a potato; beaten potato is mash

indicators.note: the two letters hold the drug's letter between them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
K is street slang for ketamine

explanation.surface: A spud pounded together with someone carrying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: W and I hold K to make WKI, which sits inside MASH. Murphy is old slang for a potato, from the Irish surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sentimental in a sickly way, and mushy is used of soppy, over-sweet feeling.

clue.text: Two birds at the outset naturally avoided tax

indicators.note: the letter is left out of the birds

parts.note: a tit and a hen are two birds

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter N

explanation.surface: Someone naturally avoiding tax, with a pair of birds thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT plus HEN loses N, the first letter of 'naturally', leaving TITHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of produce or income paid to support the church.

clue.text: One long in the water? Leave rock

parts.note: a congé is leave to depart, a dismissal
to reel is to sway or rock

explanation.surface: Someone told to quit a rock after too long in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Congé, a French word used in English for permission to leave, is unusual; 'One long' is a long fish, not a long swim.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea fish is very long and eel-shaped, so it is a long creature living in water.

clue.text: Caught by Corbynistas? Twig one faces dilemma in it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
supporters of Jeremy Corbyn are the political left
a stick is a twig

explanation.surface: Someone caught by Corbyn's fans suddenly understands their awkward position.
explanation.walkthrough: Corbynistas are followers of former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn; 'Twig' looks like the verb to realise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be 'in a cleft stick' is an idiom for being trapped between two bad choices.

clue.text: The XI bats with a real delight

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket eleven batting to the joy of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the cricket verb but is the adjective 'crazy', signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate is to make someone feel very happy and lively, a synonym of the verb to delight.

clue.text: British gun even seen in the French conflict zone

indicators.note: the poetic word is seen inside the other parts

parts.note: le is French for the
a field of battle is a conflict zone
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A British weapon spotted even on a French battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN sits between LE and FIELD. The Lee-Enfield was the standard British army rifle in both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lee-Enfield is a bolt-action rifle used by the British Army for much of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Hot sauce ordeal in mess on island: Tees hardly sated?

indicators.note: in an across answer the jumbled part comes after the island letter
letters in a mess are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter Tees on an island, suffering a fiery sauce and still hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the setter of this puzzle, so 'Tees hardly sated' means the setter is famished, speaking in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hungry person's exclamation of being ravenous, exactly what an unsatisfied appetite would say.

clue.text: Local I love — Nag's Head — enjoys majestic setting

indicators.note: the small letters enjoy a place inside the royal word
the royal word acts as a setting around the letters

parts.note: regal means majestic, kingly
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter N

explanation.surface: A pub-goer's favourite local, the Nag's Head, in grand surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's regular pub, and the Nag's Head is a common pub name; but 'Local' is the adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional means belonging to a particular area, which is what local describes.

clue.text: Prime Minister once great leader?

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782
a great in a field is a star

explanation.surface: Praise for a former Prime Minister as a great leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North led Britain through the American War of Independence; 'leader' is a guiding light, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris has long been used by navigators to find their way, so it guides travellers.

clue.text: Enthusiastic artists' clique?

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
a ring is a closed group or clique

explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is crossword shorthand for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means very eager and keen.

clue.text: Scots lad drinking gallon to establish connection

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the lad holds the letter

parts.note: loon is a Scots word for a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A Scottish youth downing a gallon to make friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Loon is a dialect word for a lad in north-east Scotland; 'connection' is to a computer system, not social.
explanation.definitionFit: To log on is to connect to a computer or network by entering credentials.

clue.text: Member for Portsmouth North, non-U, sarcastic

indicators.note: says the letter U is removed from the surname

parts.note: Penny Mordaunt was MP for Portsmouth North

explanation.surface: Describes a Conservative MP as unrefined and cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is a British term for not upper class; here it simply means without U.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit or humour is sharply critical and biting, much like sarcastic remarks.

clue.text: Decaying vegetable matter in Hebridean island

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dirt or manure, rotting organic stuff
second meaning: one of the Small Isles in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: Muck is a small island off Scotland's west coast, near Eigg and Rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck means manure or filth, and is also the name of a little Scottish isle.

clue.text: First thirteen letters? That's very small amount

parts.note: A is the first letter of the alphabet
a run of letters spans from one letter to another, so the plural supplies the linking word between the two ends
M is the thirteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about the alphabet's first half, answered by something tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The first thirteen letters run from A to M; written out, that range is the answer, with the linking TO read between the two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest particle, so the word is used for a minute quantity of anything.

clue.text: Leading monk in excellent surroundings in theory

indicators.note: the excellent letters surround the monk

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
a prior is a monk in charge of a priory

explanation.surface: A senior monk in a fine setting, thinking abstractly.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning top quality, becomes AI with 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from principles rather than observation, so it is reasoning in the abstract.

clue.text: Rant beginning to end? Say it's true!

indicators.note: the first letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: to rave is to rant wildly

explanation.surface: Someone ranting from start to finish, then pleading to be believed.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly that something is so, to assert it.

clue.text: Trick follows trick in American apartment

indicators.note: the first trick word comes after the second

parts.note: to con is to trick
to do someone is to cheat or trick them

explanation.surface: A con artist pulling one trick after another in an American flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Condo, short for condominium, is the US word for an apartment that is individually owned.

clue.text: Ribs in this lively stew kept in cold room

indicators.note: the jumbled stew is kept inside the cold room, held within its letters

parts.note: a hall is a room

indicators.note: lively letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spare ribs in a vigorous stew kept in a chilly room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ribs' reads as a meat dish in the stew, but they are the bones of a body, and the answer is the structure they form.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs form part of the thoracic body structure enclosing the lungs, so they are found there.
